messages:
mira (Support): Hey team — escalating an odd streaming issue from AcmeRetail (Dedicated / Private VPC). Customer reports that SSE streams stop delivering partial events after ~70s. Client reconnects and gets a new stream (duplicate first few tokens), which both causes a brief UX flash and is showing up as two streaming sessions in billing. Repro steps and logs below.

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): Confirmed. Happens reliably behind our corporate gateway (Windows-based proxy) but not when we hit the private endpoint from a machine inside the same VPC. If we curl from inside VPC stream is stable. From our office it cuts out mid-event.

mira (Support): Key details they provided: Dedicated node in us-west2, private control plane, VPC MTU 1500, corporate proxy doing TLS termination and HTTP/1.1 reproxying. Their proxy advertises keepalive timeout of 60s.

jen (Customer Success): @kevin can you look at any known interactions between our SSE chunking and proxies that aggregate small writes? We might be seeing the proxy coalescing small chunks into larger frames and then closing idle connection.

kevin (Infra): Noted. We have seen proxies that buffer until a buffer threshold or timeout then flush with Connection: close. Two quick things to check: (1) whether the proxy turns on response buffering (nginx proxy_buffering on) and (2) whether it rewrites Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length. If proxy inserts Content-Length it will break streaming.

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): We ran a simple curl test from office:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://dedicated-usw2.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-l"  \
  | sed -n '1,80p'
```
Output shows initial event lines then nothing. If we immediately reconnect we sometimes see the remainder, sometimes get duplicate tokens.

mira (Support): They also attached a short packet capture showing lots of 1460-byte TCP segments then a TCP FIN immediately after a small chunk containing the end of an SSE event. Their proxy is not preserving chunk boundaries. Looks symptomatic of MTU-aligned segmentation + proxy reassembly + idle timeout.

raj (SRE): Two failure modes we should consider: (A) Proxy closes idle connection causing server to not receive the client reconnect with Last-Event-ID header which would let us resume; (B) Proxy rewrites headers (adds Content-Length) causing client to think stream ended normally. Both can cause client to open a new billing session. We bill per-stream lifetime so reconnects look like separate sessions.

mira (Support): Repro steps I ran from a machine outside VPC using socat to simulate a buffering proxy:

```
# acts like a buffering middlebox that aggregates writes then forwards
socat TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork,reuseaddr PROXY:dedicated-usw2.redwood.example:443,proxyport=443,proxyprotocol=1
# then curl to localhost:8080
```
We get the same truncated SSE payload. Server logs show connection closed by peer after WRITE of ~512 bytes. No application error on server.

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): We also noticed auth behavior: when the client reconnects it sometimes uses a short-lived ephemeral token issued at reconnect and our billing shows two separate sessions because the reconnect doesn't carry previous session_id. Is there guidance to resume a stream so we don't double-bill?

kevin (Infra): On the product side the correct resume path is to include a resume token (we set session_id in the SSE initial payload and expect Last-Event-ID to be used by clients). But if a middlebox drops or strips Last-Event-ID or manipulates the Authorization header on reconnect, the server will create a fresh session. Two mitigation paths: server-side dedup (associate ephemeral tokens to a persistent session_id provided during initial handshake) or client-side: persist session_id and include it in Authorization metadata/query param on reconnect.

mira (Support): Actionables we tried with AcmeRetail and results: 
- Turn off proxy buffering (nginx: proxy_buffering off) -> streaming stable in their staging proxy.
- Increase proxy keepalive to 300s -> cuts down mid-event closes in our tests.
- Ensure proxy doesn't add Content-Length or force buffering -> resolved in many cases.

raj (SRE): Additional server-level safeguards we can propose: 
- Emit periodic 15s heartbeat SSE comment lines `: hb\n\n` to keep proxies from idling out (we already emit small pings but can make them more frequent for on-prem).
- Accept and honor a client-supplied session_id query param that will link reconnects for billing dedup if the token maps to same customer. This requires a product decision (billing implications).

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): Heartbeats helped during our quick test. We still want a durable resume because some of our clients see 90–120s of silence due to office network policies.

mira (Support): We also identified a problematic behavior: some corporate proxies convert chunked responses into buffered responses and then close connection with a FIN when their internal timeout hits. That leaves the client mid-event. When client reconnects, it doesn't always send Last-Event-ID because it was using a browser EventSource polyfill with no ability to set custom headers. That explains duplicates.

kevin (Infra): For browsers, recommended approach: use the SDK wrapper (we provide one) that uses Fetch with ReadableStream and exposes resume semantics (and allows adding session_id via query param) instead of raw EventSource. For non-browser clients, recommend Last-Event-ID header and persistent session_id.

jen (Customer Success): Customer asked for an immediate workaround they can rollout: what we recommend operationally?

mira (Support): Suggested immediate steps for AcmeRetail: 
1) Ask network team to disable proxy buffering or add a rule for streaming endpoints to set `proxy_buffering off`/`transfer-encoding: chunked` passthrough.
2) Increase proxy idle/keepalive to > 180s.
3) Add client-side session_id persisted across reconnects, include it as `?session_id=...` on the SSE URL.
4) Roll SDK that uses fetch/readableStream for browsers.

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): We applied 1+2 to our staging proxy and it's much better. Will push to production next week.

mira (Support): Followups for engineering: @kevin / @raj can you triage whether we should: 
- Add a server-side de-dup policy configurable per-customer (link reconnect tokens to session_id for billing dedup).
- Increase default ping frequency for private deployments or make it configurable.
- Add explicit guidance in Dedicated/Private onboarding docs for proxies (snippet for nginx, F5, ISA/TMG).

kevin (Infra): I'll create a small playbook PR with nginx snippets and add a flag for stronger pings in private control plane (configurable). We'll also add a quick telemetry tag when a stream is terminated by FIN from peer so we can count proxy-caused closes.

raj (SRE): I'll open an internal ticket to explore lightweight server dedup: associate ephemeral session tokens to a provided session_id and ignore new sessions within 30s of a previous stream if metadata matches (subject to billing/legal review).

mira (Support): Billing escalation: tagging @billing-team — customer flagged duplicate charge entries when reconnects happen within a single user action. We need to investigate whether we can merge short-lived reconnections before invoicing.

ops-bot: Ticket created: SUP-7439 - "AcmeRetail SSE disconnects behind corporate proxy / session dedup" assigned to infra, sre, billing.

jen (Customer Success): Thanks everyone — I'll update AcmeRetail with the staging workaround and ETA for the infra playbook.

acme-dev (AcmeRetail): Appreciate the quick help. We'll monitor after prod push. Will report back if anything else pops up.

mira (Support): Summary / next steps: 
- Customer applying proxy config changes (disable buffering, increase keepalive).
- Infra: nginx playbook + telemetry for FIN-closed streams.
- SRE: explore server-side dedup option.
- Billing: assess merge logic for short reconnects.
- Customer Success: follow up with customer in 48 hours.

(End of thread)
